title: Red Ryder
paragraphs: Western adventures based on the popular comic-strip cowboy Red Ryder, following the hero, Little Beaver, and their friends through frontier conflicts and action stories.

Juvenile Western adventure adapted from Fred Harman’s Red Ryder comic strip. Early stories used multi-part serial structure within a Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday schedule; later surviving programs are more episodic. The frozen GRH snapshot contains 65 playable/archive objects, including four without exact dates.
GRH documents the program through Red Ryder radio run (February 3, 1942 to 1951).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include land, water and property disputes, frontier law, sheriffs and crime, horses, rodeos and riding, Native American characters and frontier representation, ranching, cattle and range conflict, and gambling, robbery and financial schemes.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Comic-strip Western adapted to juvenile radio, Red Ryder Victory Patrol and wartime youth culture, 1940s juvenile-Western representation of Native American characters, and Sponsor-supported juvenile adventure radio.
